findings.evidence: The error branch renders an AlertCircle and `Error loading calendar: {error}` inside a red panel, and nothing else. The fetch function is in scope but no control in the rendered tree calls it again; the only way to retry is a full page reload.
findings.message: The calendar's error state is a dead end — it reports the failure and offers no way to try again.

findings.evidence: The cell background is `#fef2f2` when `[0, 6].includes(getDay())` OR when any event on the day is a Holiday — one colour carrying two different meanings — and `#eff6ff` for today. No legend, text or icon appears anywhere in the file to decode them.
findings.message: Weekends and holidays are marked by background colour alone, and share the same colour as each other.

findings.evidence: The event dialog renders with `fixed inset-0 bg-black/50` and `aria-modal="true"`, but the file contains no useRef, no .focus() call and no focus trap. Focus stays on the day cell behind the overlay, Tab walks out into the page underneath, and closing restores focus to nothing.
findings.message: The event dialog is modal in appearance and ARIA but never takes, holds or returns keyboard focus.

findings.evidence: `const { data, error } = await supabase...` then `if (!error && data) setNewsItems(...)`. The error is destructured and then discarded — no state is set, nothing is rendered, nothing is logged. newsItems stays [], and line 537 renders "No published news yet."
findings.message: A failed news fetch renders exactly the same screen as a school that has published no news.

findings.evidence: `if (!error) setHistoryItems((data || []).filter(...))` — the archived-news fetch discards its error the same way, and line 292 then renders "No archived news available."
findings.message: A failed archive fetch is reported to the reader as an empty archive.

findings.evidence: `const openDay = () => dateEvents.length > 0 && setSelectedEvent(dateEvents[0])` is the handler for the whole cell, while line 278 renders up to three `truncate` chips and line 290 a "+N more" count. Every chip opens dateEvents[0], so the second and later events on a day have their titles clipped and their detail unreachable by any interaction.
findings.message: On a day with more than one event, only the first is reachable — the rest are clipped chips that open somebody else's detail.
